target_claim: The constructive decomposition (components S1..Sp of G[S], T1..Tq of G[T], Cij = edges between Si and Tj) yields, for every non-empty Cij, a minimal cut (bond) of G.
source_quote:
Therefore, each non-empty Cij is a minimal cut, and we have expressed C as a disjoint
union of minimal cuts.
test_sketch: Implement the construction exactly as written (~40 lines: connected components of G[S] and G[T] via BFS, bucket cut edges into Cij). Oracle: brute-force bond checker on graphs with <= 12 vertices (a set F is a cut-set iff F = delta(A) for some vertex subset A; minimal iff no proper subset is a cut-set; equivalently check removal increases component count and every proper subset does not). Input family: 4-cycle K_{2,2} with S = {s1,s2}, T = {t1,t2}, edges s1t1, s1t2, s2t1, s2t2 and no intra-side edges. All Si and Tj are singleton components, so each non-empty Cij is a single edge of the 4-cycle; removing one edge of a 4-cycle leaves the graph connected, so the oracle reports that Cij is not even a cut-set, refuting the quoted claim. Randomized small bipartite-ish partitions would surface many more such failures.
